our-mission.title: Our Mission
our-mission.body:
Our Mission

Proclaiming the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ to those who have never heard and stirring churches to greater evangelistic and missions outreach. It doesn’t matter who you are or where you are on your life’s journey, you are most welcome here. We believe in transformation, we believe the church’s mission is changing lives – individually and globally. We support, encourage and uplift small groups where lives are being changed through the Word of God, Worship, Fellowship, and Christian Discipleship. We are committed for the advancement of the Kingdom of God through global partnerships and missionaries. Gifts to Our Church benefit the full range of the Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Toronto’s mission here and in Ethiopia.

"Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. --- Matthew 28:19-20"

Deeper Relationship with God

Our mission is to encourage our members to keep moving towards a deeper and intimate relationship with God through Jesus Christ, creating disciples so that the church can be equipped to live as God commanded, helping the needy by using the gifts that God has given to serve him. We train and prepare leaders committed to serve God in ministry in the present and future church.

And what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.--- 2 Timothy 2:2

Our Missions in Ethiopia

Besides reaching out souls and impacting the Ethiopian Community in Toronto, the Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Toronto is supporting a large mission work known us Mission Geregema since 1994. The church’s missionary, Binora Dado has been laboring in Gewada (Tsemha) region of Southern Nations and Nationalities state of Ethiopia – bringing a total transformation to his community.

By the power of the Gospel of Jesus Christ and the continual mission support of EECT, thousands have come to Christ and over thirty three churches established in many localities of the region. Side by side with the preaching of the gospel, various measures of community development works were implemented which include: flour mill, schools, water supply wells with a reservoir through gravitational system.

statement-of-faith.title: What We Believe
statement-of-faith.body:
In God - existing eternally in three persons: God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

  • Jesus is the Son of God and God Himself
  • We believe that mankind is created in the image of God, but totally deprived after the Great Fall
  • We believe that there is no hope for mankind apart from the Gospel of Jesus Christ
  • Jesus is the Way the Truth and the Life for Salvation and thereby to have relationship with the Father.
  • We can only be saved by grace through Faith in Jesus Christ
  • Every born again Christian must live for the Glory of God in the power of the Holy Spirit

We believe in the authority of the Scripture

We believe that the entire Bible is the Word of God. written by men, inspired through the Holy Spirit. The Bible is therefore without error in its original manuscripts. It is God’s unique revelation to mankind and infallible Word of God. The Bible is the supreme and final authority in matters of faith and life and therefore without error in what it teaches and affirms. No other writings are vested with such divine authority

The purpose of the church is to make Christ known to lost men & women

We believe that the Church is the body of Christ consisted of all born-again believers. Jesus Christ is the Head of the Church, His Body, which is composed of all believers; the living and the dead, who have been joined to Him through Saving Faith as taught in the Gospel. We believe God has called the church to conform to the image of Christ, to care for its members and evangelize the world. Since all members of the body of Christ are united in Christ by the same Spirit, it is imperative for them to live in love, harmony, and unity.

im-new-here.title: FAQ
im-new-here.body:
Welcome. We are glad you found us! Being a part of a new church is exciting. Please know that we are equally excited to have you here at Ethiopian Evangelical Church in Toronto. We hope you find a warm, hospitable, and fun filled environment where you can connect with others and build your faith in Jesus Christ.

No Matter Who you are...You Are Welcome Here..

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I have to be a member of the church to attend the service?

No. You are not required to be a member of the church to attend service. Though our service is conducted in Amharic and therefore knowledge of Amharic is desired, nevertheless, translators could be assigned upon request. Our church welcomes people from all walks of life.

What can I expect when I am here?

When you arrive you will be greeted and may be given a bulletin that contains details of the entire service. We also project the service on an overhead screen. Our Ushers are happy to answer any questions you might have.

At Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Toronto we seek to blend the best of both the ancient and modern expressions of Christian worship. We sing Amharic hymns written some decades ago, and we sing songs of praise written recently. Our choir is a part of our worship experience each week.

The Word of our God is central to our worship. Our pastors and lay preachers generally preach through a portion of a Bible book in Amharic. Each week then - we seek to understand and apply the truth contained in a particular passage of Scripture.

Do you have a dress code?

You don’t have to be in your “Sunday’s Best”. We want you to be comfortable in what you are wearing. Some people dress casually, some dress culturally. We don’t believe that certain clothes are inherently more spiritual than others. But through our dress and even our appearance we want to display modesty to glorify God our father.

What are the timings for your services and other activities?

We have bible studies and various teaching classes at our center beginning from 1pm on Sunday. Our Sunday afternoon worship service begins at 3pm. For a complete listing of activities, including activities on Sunday and Wednesday evenings, please check out our weekly schedule here.

Do you provide childcare for my children?"

Yes. Nursery is provided for children under 2 years old. We have dedicated childcare providers on site who will look after your children. We also have Sunday school classes for all children according to their ages. Parents could also volunteer to help Sunday school teachers.

If your children are under 4 years old, we expect you to bring following items in a baby care bag:

  1. Diapers
  2. Formula
  3. Wipe clothes
  4. Dress clothes
 

Do you have Sunday school for children?

Yes we do. Our children ministry provides biblical teaching through Sunday school classes. Our Children’s ministry is divided in to 2 group based on their age.

  1. Grade 1 to 7 is in one group
  2. Grade 8 to 12 is another group

These 2 groups are taught by experienced volunteers who taught in our church for long time and well versed in God’s word.

What about parking?

Ethiopian Evangelical Church is located at 2275 Markham Road, Scarborough ON. Parking is FREE on the premises.

Handicapped Parking?

Handicapped parking is available in the lot in the front of the building. If you need assistance while upon entering our parking lot, ushers & volunteers are available at the designated lot.

Am I allowed to take part in church activities, ministries etc.,?

Yes. We are always looking for a member to play on active roles in church activities. We have many ministry groups and opportunities that you can invest your expertise and time for the glory of God. Please contact one of our ministers and discuss your interest. They will be glad to give you more information. Or click here to fill out the contact form.  Someone will get back to you.

Do you encourage small groups such as bible study and prayer meetings?

Yes. In fact, we have zonal fellowships in various locations in the city. Many of our members host home bible study fellowships and prayer meetings in their own homes during the week-days and weekends. We believe these groups provide invaluable strength to our church members and visitors. These home fellowship groups are found across the city.

If you are interested to join one of the home bible study fellowships or prayer meetings, please contact one of the elders or fill out the contact form to get started.

Is donation or tithe mandatory?

For those who are born-again believers and members of the church, it is imperative to faithfully give their offering and tithes. However, newcomers or visitors are not expected to do so unless they want to donate in their own free will for missions of the church. In return, we hope that the Word, worship, and Fellowship will be a gift to you.

All donations and tithes received goes towards our mission here in Toronto and also in Ethiopia in the form of church planting, supporting Evangelists, opening new schools, providing water wells and other necessities for the community in need.

More Questions?

pastoral-care.title: Pastoral Care
pastoral-care.body:
This Ministry department is one of the major Ministry departments of the E.E.Church in Toronto. It was established, two years after the reunification of the three Churches in 2002, when we three pastors got ordained to serve the Lord, Jesus Christ, and His Church.

Counseling in the secular setting is the use of various techniques to help a person solve a conflict or better his life adjustment. However, Biblical Counseling is part of Spiritual support to our Members, and others who seek our help.

Counseling

There are some basic reasons why counseling is so important. One is that it focuses on the needs of individuals. Yes, Pulpit preaching is indeed a blessing, but it may not always meet One’s specific needs

The importance and significance of Counseling is to address human needs; such as loneliness, discouragement, doubt, grief, sadness, envy, violence, poverty, sickness, interpersonal tensions, and variety of other personal problems. The other reason for the need of counseling includes, escalating Family crisis. This is the most exhibited problem in the lives of many immigrant families, who came from a lot of traumatic situations, due to hardship and abuses, they all faced.

Most Pastors realize the importance of the Pulpit ministry but some have not fully considered the significance of counseling ministry. It has been said that a minister who doesn’t place a strong emphasis on counseling is only “ half a minister.” That is why the board of Elders (Pastors and Elders of E.E.C.), being led by the Holy Spirit made a curtail decision to have a counseling department for our Church.

Goals of Biblical Counseling:

1. To provide Abundant Life, in all its fullness to individuals, through having Belief in Jesus Christ, here on Earth.

2. To provide eternal hope, through pointing individuals to the Eternal Life in Heaven. (Jn.3:16).

3. To minister healing or therapy using the principles of the Word of God.

4. Change is the main Goal in all Biblical Counseling

  • Everyone of us know and agree that change in life is not easy and at times very difficult. Stopping any habits such as smoking, overcoming Anger, controlling temper, losing weight and starting new habits are not easy.
  • Eliminating the problem can not be the goal of counseling. Helping the person to personal happiness either is not the goal of counseling.
  • Most Christians are either unwilling or do not know how to make thechange that God requires of them.

5. Changing the past is not the goal either.

  • We need to forget the past, and not even attempt to change it (Philip. 3:13-14).
  • It is the counselee who needs to be changed, and not his/her past. However, the counselor can only deal with the past guilt that is involved in the past.
  • The counselee can be assured a better future by making behaviour and personality change in the present
  • The counsellor must call for repentance, a change of mind that leads to a change of life. True change in life follows true repentance that the Holy Spirit always brings to that life. (2cor.7:10)

6. To be changed to the likeness of Jesus Christ is the Final goal.

We don’t see change that sticks because of the repetition of sin one’s life that becomes habitual. The repetitive, habitual pattern of sin, needs genuine repentance, confession and forgiveness. Then we can say one is justified and through sanctification will continuously grow to the likeness of Jesus Christ.

More Questions?

Ushers & Greeters are the first members of the church to greet and welcome the congregation. Their smile, warmth and love reflect the church’s joy of having you worshipping with us. They are courteous and kind, yet stern. They give a smile and a warm welcome to brighten each ones day. about-us.title: About Us
about-us.body:
The congregation of the Ethiopian Evangelical Church is mainly made up of warm and loving, born-again Christians of Ethiopian & Eritrean origin. Our mission is to carry out the great commission of Jesus Christ as recorded in Matt. 28, to reach out the Ethiopian community with the Gospel of Jesus Christ in their language, to provide development programs geared toward the well-being of the community.

The Church’s spiritual need is carried out jointly by the pastors and the board of Elders – as overseers. While the Worship service of the main congregation is done in the Amharic language, full-fledged English service is held side by side. We have services, prayer meetings and home fellowships throughout the week. Please refer our services page for more details.

HISTORY

In the wake of Ethiopian military coup of 1974, thousands were killed for their views and most of the time without any substantial reason under Stalinist motto - the “Red Terror.” The Church was persecuted heavily – particularly evangelical believers. Closing churches, imprisoning and torturing Christian leaders and the youth was daily ordeal believers faced. As a result hundreds of thousands were forced to flee to neighboring countries – the Sudan, Kenya, and Djibouti – and from there to Europe, the United States, and Canada

Following such a massive migration, some Ethiopians came to Canada as early as 1985. Ethiopians who were settled in Toronto area established churches in different municipalities. Later, Elders of 3 of those churches came together and prayed to God for his guidance to bring these churches together. Thus, the three churches: Bethlehem, Full Gospel, & Ethiopian Evangelical churches that were serving the community in Toronto were united in 1999

VISION

Our vision is to pursue a living relationship with God through our faith in Christ; to know Christ and make Him known and nurture believers by the Word of God through various church services.

Besides reaching out souls and impacting the Ethiopian Community in Toronto, the EECT is supporting a large mission work known as Mission Geregema in southern Ethiopia since 1994. By the power of the Gospel of Jesus Christ and the continual mission support of the Ethiopian Evangelical Church in Toronto, thousands have come to Christ and over thirty three local churches established in many localities of the region. Side by side with the preaching of the gospel, various measures of community development works are also applied to improve the life of the community. We envision bringing the gospel to the people and equipping them to serve the Lord.

OUR MISSION

Proclaiming the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ to those who have never heard and stirring churches to greater evangelistic and missions outreach. It doesn’t matter who you are or where you are on your life’s journey, you are most welcome here. We believe in transformation, we believe the church’s mission is changing lives – individually and globally. We support, encourage and uplift small groups where lives are being changed through the Word of God, Worship, Fellowship, and Christian Discipleship. We are committed for the advancement of the Kingdom of God through global partnerships and missionaries. Gifts to Our Church benefit the full range of the Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Toronto’s mission here and in Ethiopia.

“Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. — Matthew 28:19-20“
Deeper Relationship with God

Our mission is to encourage our members to keep moving towards a deeper and intimate relationship with God through Jesus Christ, creating disciples so that the church can be equipped to live as God commanded, helping the needy by using the gifts that God has given to serve him. We train and prepare leaders committed to serve God in ministry in the present and future church.

And what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.— 2 Timothy 2:2

Our Missions in Ethiopia

Besides reaching out souls and impacting the Ethiopian Community in Toronto, the Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Toronto is supporting a large mission work known us Mission Geregema since 1994. The church’s missionary, Binora Dado has been laboring in Gewada (Tsemha) region of Southern Nations and Nationalities state of Ethiopia – bringing a total transformation to his community.

By the power of the Gospel of Jesus Christ and the continual mission support of EECT, thousands have come to Christ and over thirty three churches established in many localities of the region. Side by side with the preaching of the gospel, various measures of community development works were implemented which include: flour mill, schools, water supply wells with a reservoir through gravitational system.

VALUES

We are a community called to reach-out and demonstrate the love and grace of Jesus through our lives and words – both here in our community and around the world. We are a community called to reach up as believers, loving and worshiping God at our most highest. The foundations of this church are Biblical teaching of the Word, Spirit-led worship, authentic relationships, unceasing prayer, and compassionate provision for the needy

Christianity is not a set of religious rules but a living relationship with the Triune God in Jesus Christ. Our focus as a church is to respond to His calling on our lives. Having been saved and connected to Him through saving-faith of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, we now serve our Savior with gladness. The Gospel motivates us to worship Jesus, to obey and follow Him every day. It also drives us to share God’s love with our families, friends, community, and the world at large.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”

— John 1:1

about-our-pastoral-staff.title: About Our Pastoral Staff
about-our-pastoral-staff.body:
The movement of the Holy Spirit swept the entire country of Ethiopia in 1967. This captured the attention of many young and old who were hungry for god. One of them was young Alemayehu Gondere who was serving the Ethiopian Air Force. During those excited times, Full Gospel Church was born where thousands of souls got saved as a result of Gospel preaching.

Knowing God in Christ Jesus, gave Alemayehu Gondere not only everlasting life, but new perspective, and fresh outlook to life here on Earth. Since this wonderful spiritual blessing, God in His Omnipresence has been always with him and my family to this day. Before coming to Canada, he was engaged in spreading the Gospel. Alemayehu was small Group that started the first Ethiopian Christians Fellowship, at first Baptist Church, which grew to the biggest Ethiopian Evangelical Church, Pastored by the three servants of the Lord.

As a Born again Believer, Dr Alemayehu Gondere got blessed in many ways, spiritually and as well as professionally. He was also blessed with Marriage and have had three children. Recently he & his wife are blessed with a grand child

Born into a religious family with many generations of devoted ministers in the Bethe-kihnet tradition, Dr. Efrem Leakemariam was expected to follow the status quo. He grew up listening and observing religious teaching at home. Because Efrem’s father was a Pastor, his home was always filed with full of hymn and daily chanting.

Even though Efrem was involved in religious activities and Deacon in the most revered church of Ethiopia, he always felt empty inside. His soul was searching something to fill the void and gain some inner peace. Once he traveled almost 80 km on foot to the Monastery of Debre-Damo and stayed with a number of Monks and Hermits for weeks.

Turning point came in the form of a Christian man who was travelling in the area, with whom he had deep religious conversation. Efrem learned the need of salvation, meaning of scriptures. Especially Acts 4:12 “Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved”. Soon after that conversation, Efrem was beginning to feel the presence of Holy Spirit in his life.

Dr Efrem had served in different capacities: as an elder, bible study leader, counselor, mission board leader, and also in teaching & preaching the Word of God together with many dear brothers & sisters. He was called to the Pastoral Ministry and ordained together with other brothers on May 4, 2002 in Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Toronto.

In the wake of Ethiopian military coup in 1974, which followed by "Red Terror". Thousands were killed for their views and most of the time without any substantial reason. The Church was persecuted heavily - particularly evangelical believers. Closing churches, imprisoning and torturing Christian leaders and the youth was daily ordeal believers faced. As a result hundreds of thousands were forced to flee to neighboring countries - the Sudan, Kenya, and Djibouti - and from there to Europe, the United States, and Canada.

Following such a massive migration, some Ethiopians came to Canada as early as 1985. Ethiopians who were settled in Toronto area established churches in different communities. Elders in 3 of those churches came together and prayed god for his guidance to bring these churches together. In 1999, God’s spiritual guidance brought together three full Gospel, Evangelical churches that were serving Ethiopian communities in Toronto.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”

— John 1:1

family-ministry-2.title: Board of Elders
family-ministry-2.body:
OFFICE OF THE BOARD OF ELDERS

The office of the board of Elders is based on several scriptural passages principally on I Timothy 3:1-7, and I Peter 5:1-11. The office of Elders is also mentioned in Ephesus during Paul’s third missionary journey (Acts 20:17-19). At the Ethiopian Evangelical Church in Toronto, there are seven elders elected by the general assembly of all members of the church every three years. They are in charge of administrative decisions in the life of the Church - responsible for various activities within the congregation.

EECT’s Elders are servants, not Lords. They do not rule as authorities in hierarchy because all authority belongs to Christ alone, who is the head of the Church. The Elders’ role is therefore supervisory, advisory, and making important decisions where it is necessary. Elders are instrumental, through their individual and family life, leadership, teaching - bringing about consensus in the assembly according the Scripture. All members — including elders — submit to the Lord Jesus Christ, then to one another. In other words, there is no chain of command — but only a network of submission. Those who humble themselves to the level of servant-hood before the Lord and His assembly may be raised to the level of true accountability in the Church.

members.title: New Members
members.body:
Welcome to the Ethiopian Evangelical Church in Toronto, where we are committed to building a community of believers in Jesus Christ. As a church that is primarily made up of Ethiopians and Eritreans, we strive to create a welcoming environment that reflects our unique cultural heritage while also celebrating our shared faith.

If you are interested in becoming a member of our church, please fill out our registration form. Your personal information will be kept confidential and used only for church-related purposes.

Our church offers a variety of opportunities for worship, fellowship, and service, including:

  • Amharic and English language services
  • Bible studies and small group gatherings
  • Youth and children's ministries
  • Women's and men's ministries
  • Outreach programs to the Ethiopian and Eritrean communities in Toronto

We believe that everyone is called to serve in some capacity, and we encourage all members to use their unique gifts and talents to build up the church and serve others.

Thank you for considering the Ethiopian Evangelical Church in Toronto as your spiritual home. We look forward to getting to know you and sharing in the joy of fellowship and worship together.
